title: Finite Gibbs-isometric Duhamel remainder
question: Can the all-time orbit-bound hypothesis in the finite-member Duhamel bridge be removed for each fixed finite Gibbs Hamiltonian, while keeping volume-uniformity and OS identification explicitly open?

finite_time_theorem.setup: Let H=H* be finite dimensional, rho_beta=Z^(-1) exp(-beta H), alpha_t(X)=U_t* X U_t with U_t=exp(-itH/hbar), and delta_H(X)=(i/hbar)[H,X].
finite_time_theorem.identity: Finite-dimensional differentiation gives R_t(X)=integral from 0 to t of (t-s) alpha_s(delta_H^2(X)) ds.
finite_time_theorem.bound: Gibbs isometry and the triangle inequality give N_beta(R_t(X)) <= t^2 N_beta(delta_H^2(X))/2 for t>=0, with no separate all-time orbit envelope assumption.
finite_time_theorem.orientation: The same statement applies independently to each finite orientation sigma; comparing orientations in one OS carrier still requires the missing intertwiner.

finding.finite: For each fixed finite Gibbs member the exact Duhamel remainder is bounded by t^2/2 times the finite double-commutator seminorm; the prior all-time orbit hypothesis is unnecessary at this finite level.
finding.thermodynamic: The double-commutator seminorm may depend on volume, source, cutoff and orientation, so this does not close a uniform direct D or delta-D Cauchy estimate.
finding.os: The result does not identify finite members with the fixed-beta OS mixture or supply a common Hamiltonian generator.

scope.not_closed: The fixed finite-member remainder bound is not a thermodynamic or OS theorem. Uniform double-commutator control, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion, common alpha, KMS/GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.

adversarial_review.check: The generator delta_H=(i/hbar)[H,·] is used consistently; the second commutator fixture is checked with the complex factor and its norm is sign-independent.
Gibbs invariance follows from rho_beta being a function of the same H, not from an arbitrary fixed state.
The t^2/2 identity is a finite-dimensional Bochner/Taylor identity and does not assume a uniform-in-time orbit constant.
Each finite orientation has its own Gibbs seminorm and double commutator; no equality between plus and minus members is assumed.
No volume/source/cutoff uniformity is inferred from finite-dimensional finiteness.
R248 checks exact rational matrix-entry and seminorm fixtures, not unbounded domains or a limit theorem.
No OS/KMS identification, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A conclusion follows.
This is a positive finite theorem and creates no new global negative result.

qft_interface.closed: An exact fixed finite Gibbs Duhamel remainder bound with the all-time orbit-envelope hypothesis removed at finite volume.
qft_interface.open: Uniform double-commutator estimates, actual Q3 history, direct D/delta-D, finite-to-OS identification, common alpha, KMS/GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: No heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner is supplied.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing fixed finite-member QFT interface theorem. It is not a thermodynamic limit, an OS reconstruction, or a Clay-level result.
next_action: Estimate the finite double commutator uniformly in volume/source/cutoff on the actual Q3 common core, or record an exact growth obstruction; only then revisit direct D and delta-D Cauchy.
